title: A carried-over batch is offered next session
asA: operator whose session ended before the ask fired
iWant: the SessionEnd hook to flush a bundle idempotently and the SessionStart hook of the next session to inject a one-line context reminder that pending entries exist
soThat: a crash or /clear does not lose findings and the next session's first pause carries the ask

acceptanceCriteria.description: rcf feedback hook session-end writes the outbox bundle for any pending entries under 1 second (the shared Claude Code SessionEnd budget is 1.5s) and is byte-idempotent (same content hash means no rewrite). Codex SessionEnd runs the same handler; output is discarded either way.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture with two pending entries and a stubbed clock so the elapsed time is measurable
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf feedback hook session-end is run twice back-to-back
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first run writes one bundle file under outbox; the second run runs to completion in under 1 second without rewriting the same-hash file; both exit 0

acceptanceCriteria.description: rcf feedback hook session-start with pending entries and a new sessionId prints one plain line to stdout on Claude Code ("rcf feedback: <n> unsubmitted entr(y|ies) carried over from an earlier session; ask the operator once at a natural pause (RULE 17).") and the Codex-shaped equivalent under --harness codex. The line is what the harness injects as context; it never blocks. If SessionStart on Codex cannot inject context (verified at build time against the current Codex reference), the fallback in RULE 17 ("check rcf feedback status at session start") is what carries the same posture.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture with two pending entries carried over from a prior sessionId
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf feedback hook session-start is run under each harness
acceptanceCriteria.then: the Claude Code stdout matches the exact wording above; the Codex JSON matches the reference shape currently accepted for SessionStart context; both return exit 0; state.json is not mutated (asked is set on Stop, not on session-start)

acceptanceCriteria.description: rcf feedback defer means "not now, ask again next session" (design 3.1). Entries in status deferredUntilSession whose stored sessionId is not the current one are requeued to pending on the SessionStart hook AND on the Stop hook (belt to the SessionStart braces, so the flow works when only Stop is installed). The requeue appends one state-transition line per entry with status pending and no sessionId field, so fold-by-id preserves the entry's prior sessionId and the carry-over gate in both hooks (pending.sessionId !== currentSessionId) fires naturally in the new session. Entries recorded or last deferred under the current sessionId are not re-transitioned (idempotent per session; deferring twice in one session is a no-op on the second call).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture with one pending entry deferred in session A (entries.jsonl carries the deferredUntilSession line with sessionId A)
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf feedback hook session-start --harness claude-code is run with session_id B, then rcf feedback hook stop --harness claude-code is run with the same session_id B
acceptanceCriteria.then: SessionStart appends one { status: pending } transition (no sessionId field) so the entry returns to pending with its sessionId still A; the carry-over line prints to stdout naming the count and RULE 17; the following Stop exits 2 with the ask on stderr and appends exactly one asked record for session B; a second SessionStart in session B is a no-op (no new transition, silent stdout); a further SessionStart in a fresh session_id C after a Stop-only path (no SessionStart wired) still requeues on the Stop hook so the ask fires there

acceptanceCriteria.description: [must-not] A feedback entry recorded in a linked git worktree is never lost with the worktree and never left where the main checkout would commit it. The queue of a linked worktree lives in the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/ (the round 1 storage choice). An entry rcf feedback add records in a linked worktree is offered from the main checkout after git worktree remove. A queue the worktree already holds in its own .rcf/feedback/ (as 0.36.0 left it) is moved into the main checkout's store by the next rcf feedback command run in the worktree (any sub-verb, the Stop, SessionEnd and SessionStart hooks included) once the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, so no entry, old or new, is lost when the worktree is removed, and each keeps its id (listed once) and its status. While the main checkout does not ignore .rcf/feedback/, nothing moves: rcf feedback list and the hooks in that worktree keep reading its own held queue (the Stop hook keeps asking about its pending entries), and rcf feedback add there without --force exits 2, stderr naming .rcf/feedback, rcf doctor --fix and the main checkout's directory and saying "the held entries move into the main checkout once it ignores .rcf/feedback/", and writes nothing under either checkout's .rcf/feedback/; once the main checkout ignores the store, the next rcf feedback command in the worktree moves the held queue as above. If the move fails (for example the main checkout's .rcf/ is not writable), the command exits non-zero with stderr naming the error the move hit and the main checkout's directory, nothing is written to the worktree's queue and nothing the worktree already holds is removed. The gitignore pre-write check of rcf feedback add runs against the checkout that holds the store: when the main checkout's .gitignore does not cover .rcf/feedback/, rcf feedback add in the worktree without --force refuses as AC-15501-2 refuses (exit 2, stderr names the missing .rcf/feedback/ entry, rcf doctor --fix and the main checkout's directory) and nothing is created under either checkout's .rcf/feedback/. When the main checkout does not hold the rcf project (rcf adopted on the worktree's branch only), rcf feedback add in the worktree never leaves a file the main checkout would commit; keeping the entry in the worktree or refusing is the builder's choice, and that worktree's queue surviving its removal is out of scope. Worktrees of a bare repository and separate-git-dir worktrees are out of scope. AC-15501-1 and AC-15501-2 are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a git repository holding an rcf project whose .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, and a linked worktree made with git worktree add; variants: (2) the worktree already holds a .rcf/feedback/ queue with one pending and one discarded entry, and the main checkout holds one pending entry of its own; (3) the main checkout's .gitignore does not cover .rcf/feedback/ while the worktree branch's .gitignore does; (4) the main checkout does not hold the rcf project, adopted on the worktree branch only; (5) the worktree holds a .rcf/feedback/ queue with one pending and one discarded entry while the main checkout's .gitignore does not cover .rcf/feedback/ and the worktree branch's .gitignore does; (6) the worktree holds that queue, the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/ and the main checkout's .rcf/ directory is not writable
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf feedback add (no --force) records one entry from the worktree (in variant 2 this is the next rcf feedback command run there); in the base case and variant 2 the worktree is then removed with git worktree remove (no --force); in variant 5 rcf feedback list --all --json, rcf feedback hook stop --harness claude-code with a new session_id and rcf feedback add (no --force) are each run in the worktree, then the main checkout's .gitignore gains .rcf/feedback/, rcf feedback add records one entry from the worktree and the worktree is removed with git worktree remove (no --force); in variant 6 rcf feedback add (no --force) is run in the worktree
acceptanceCriteria.then: rcf feedback list --json run from the main checkout lists that entry by id with status pending, and rcf feedback list there prints its id; in variant 2 rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists every entry the worktree held, the new entry and the main checkout's own, each id exactly once with the status it had (the discarded one stays discarded), and git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all there lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; in variant 3 the add exits 2, stderr names .rcf/feedback, rcf doctor --fix and the main checkout's directory, nothing is created under either checkout's .rcf/feedback/, and git status in the main checkout lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; in variant 4 git status in the main checkout lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/, and an entry the add accepts (exit 0) is listed pending from the worktree, while a refusal exits 2; in variant 5, before the main checkout ignores the store, rcf feedback list --all --json in the worktree lists both held entries with the status they had, the Stop hook exits 2 with the ask counting the held pending entry, the add exits 2 with stderr naming .rcf/feedback, rcf doctor --fix, the main checkout's directory and "the held entries move into the main checkout once it ignores .rcf/feedback/", the worktree's entries.jsonl is byte-identical, nothing is created under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/ and git status there lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; after the main checkout ignores the store the add exits 0 and, after git worktree remove, rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists both held entries and the new one, each id once with its status; in variant 6 the add exits non-zero, stderr names the error the move hit (EACCES) and the main checkout's directory, the worktree's .rcf/feedback/ is byte-identical to before (no new entry, nothing removed) and nothing is written under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/
